text:
mira: Heads-up — customer Elysia reporting a telemetry gap after we merged their LoRA adapter. Their dashboard shows token-level latency spikes that don't match our infra traces. Anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:
sam: I ran a quickpack earlier on our 4-bit profile. Latency looked fine here, but we did see a 3-5% drop in exact-match for numeric extraction on their eval set. saved logs: s3://redwood-debug/elysia/quickpack-4276.log
alan: Can you paste the eval summary? :eyes:
mira: eval summary (toplines):
- prompts: 150
- EM invoice numbers: baseline 92.4% -> 88.1% (drop 4.3)
- mean token latency: baseline 18ms -> reported 30ms (customer)
- 95p tail: +28ms
- quant: 4-bit QWKS profile
sam: hmm. Their adapter replaces a small portion of token embeddings with a special field token (<INV>). If tokenizer mapping is off we can see mismatch + extra detokenization work. Also prefix/KV cache behaviour changes tail latency.
tara: Could be two things: tokenizer tokenmap mismatch OR adapter introduces longer decode loop for numeric patches. Did we run the same tokenizer version as the customer?
mira: customer said they built their adapter against tokenizer v2.0.0 while our hosted runtime uses v2.0.1 (minor) — should be backward compatible but can change token ids for custom tokens.
alan: Quick repro: run smoke eval with their adapter and force tokenizer v2.0.0 in our sandbox, and disable KV-cache to see per-token runtime. Command I used previously:
```bash
python -m redwood.eval run \--model=redwood/llama-elysia-lora \--adapter=elysia-lora.safetensors \--tokenizer-version=2.0.0 \--quant=4bit \--disable-kv-cache \--pack=customers/elysia/quickpack.json
```
sam: started that locally, seeding 2 runs. Initial glance: disabling kv-cache reduced the mismatch in tail latency but overall latency still ~+10ms vs baseline. Numeric EM still down ~4%.
mira: deploy-bot: kicked a trace capture for the cloud instance handling Elysia traffic so we can correlate traces to their telemetry.
deploy-bot: Trace capture initiated for trace-id=trc-elysia-4276. Will attach when complete.
tara: Also add a lightweight tokenizer diff to the eval pack: token id histogram for all special tokens + mapping for <INV>. If ids differ by >1% we should reject adapter merge.
alan: good call. I'll add a small check step to the quickpack harness. PR incoming.
sam: If tokenizer mismatch not the root cause, next hypothesis is quantization sensitivity: LoRA fused weights + 4-bit quant can amplify small embedding offsets. Try 8-bit or quant-linear profile as fallback and run same pack.
mira: Plan: (1) run smokepack with tokenizer=2.0.0 + kv-cache off (sam/alan) (ETA 25m) (2) add token-id diff to pack (alan) (3) run fallback 8-bit quant profile overnight and generate detailed EM/FP/FN diff (sam) (4) tell customer to hold traffic on that adapter until we confirm. I'll ping legal/comms if needed.
tara: tagging me on the PR for the token-id check. If we see >1% mismatch, we should block the merge and request remap. :thumbsup:
sam: noted. I'll post the first run logs here once complete. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
mira: thanks — appreciate the quick triage everyone.
alan: if run shows adapter is the culprit, we can offer them a tiny shim that maps <INV> to the hosted token id and re-quantize — less friction than forcing them to rebuild.
mira: agreed. will keep this thread as the single source of truth, will update with logs/trace links. :white_check_mark:
